22.query: What is the primary purpose of a postincident analysis (PIA) in the context of Module 7?

positive_judgments.section: POSTINCIDENT ANALYSIS / INTRODUCTION / Definition
positive_judgments.text_excerpt: Definition The postincident analysis (PIA) is a reconstruction of an operation to determine the events that occurred, the strategy and tactics identified, the tasks chosen, and the results of the operation.

positive_judgments.section: POSTINCIDENT ANALYSIS / Purpose
positive_judgments.text_excerpt: Purpose The main purpose of the PIA is to reinforce departmental procedures and successful actions taken, and to identify ways to improve the effectiveness of operations. Simply, it catalogs what worked and the areas that need to be improved.

positive_judgments.section: POSTINCIDENT ANALYSIS / POSTINCIDENT ANALYSIS MEETING
positive_judgments.text_excerpt: POSTINCIDENT ANALYSIS MEETING The PIA meeting should be held in a room large enough to accommodate the attendees comfortably. Small rooms and cramped conditions are not conducive to having people "open up." All supporting materials from the incident should be part of the presentation, e.g., actual incident resource status sheets, dispatch audiotapes, dispatch run cards, chronology of resources dispatched and arrival times, any videotapes, slides, or prints of the incident scene, and an easel pad

positive_judgments.section: POSTINCIDENT ANALYSIS / Purpose / Attitude
positive_judgments.text_excerpt: Attitude Management needs to understand that improvement develops from analysis of what went wrong, more than from analysis of what was right. A review of an incident is a search for the opportunity to become more effective. A PIA is not a search for guilt. It is not a punishment tool. It is not intended to embarrass personnel. A PIA is an opportunity for everyone to tell what happened from his/her own perspective.

positive_judgments.section: POSTINCIDENT ANALYSIS / DESIRED OUTCOMES OF THE POSTINCIDENT ANALYSIS / Improve Performance
positive_judgments.text_excerpt: Improve Performance This is the goal of the PIA meeting. This is the one opportunity after an incident to identify those areas that need improvement. Do not take this lightly. Trivializing the recommendations given during the PIA meeting may compromise the effectiveness of the PIA.
